steps: Set the bar in a rack at about upper-chest height. Step up to it with your feet about hip-width apart and grab it with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), a little wider than your shoulders.
Lift the bar off the hooks so it rests on the front of your shoulders, just below your chin. Your elbows should point slightly forward, not out to the sides.
Take a breath and tighten your stomach and buttocks, so your body is one stiff column from your feet to your shoulders.
Press the bar straight up. As it passes your face, lean your head back slightly out of the way, then push your head forward again once the bar is past.
Finish with your arms straight and the bar directly over the middle of your feet, with your head slightly forward of the bar.
Lower the bar slowly back to your shoulders in the same straight line.
watchFor: Don't lean back or arch your lower back to push the weight up. If you have to, it's too heavy. Keep your ribs down and your stomach tight.
Start with just the empty bar. Overhead weight is much harder to control than it looks.
Never do this with a weight you can't fully control. If you get stuck, lower the bar to your shoulders and set it back on the rack.

steps: Set the bar in a rack at about upper-chest height. Grab it with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), a little wider than your shoulders, and lift it off the hooks so it rests on the front of your shoulders.
Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, elbows pointing slightly forward, chest up.
Bend your knees slightly, as if you were about to start sitting down, keeping your body upright.
Then push through your feet and straighten your legs quickly. Use that push to help drive the bar upward, and keep pressing with your arms until they are straight overhead.
Stand tall with the bar directly above the middle of your feet.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders under control while your knees bend slightly to absorb it, and get ready for the next one.
watchFor: The knee bend should be small and quick. Don't lean forward or arch your lower back.
Start light and learn the timing with the empty bar first. The leg push and the arm push must connect smoothly.
If the bar drifts forward or you feel strain in your lower back, lower the weight.

steps: Sit on a bench with the back set upright, with your back firmly supported. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward.
Put both feet flat on the floor and tighten your stomach.
Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are almost straight and the weights are above your shoulders.
Pause for a moment, then lower them slowly back to shoulder height.
watchFor: Don't arch your back or let your lower back come off the bench.
Keep your wrists straight, stacked over your elbows.
Don't clang the dumbbells together at the top. Stop when they're near each other.

steps: Sit on a bench with the back set upright and your back supported. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at chest height, with your palms facing you and your elbows in front of your body.
As you start pressing up, slowly turn your palms outward so they face forward by the time your arms are almost straight above you.
Pause at the top with the dumbbells above your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells slowly, turning your palms back toward you as they come down to chest height.
watchFor: Use lighter weights than you would for a plain press. The twisting adds strain on the shoulders.
Keep the turn smooth and controlled, not jerky.
Keep your back against the bench and don't arch.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand, resting by your sides with your palms facing your body.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your chest lifted.
Raise both arms out to your sides until they're about level with your shoulders. Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Pause at the top, then lower them slowly back to your sides.
watchFor: Use light weights. This muscle is small, and heavy weights make you swing your body.
Don't lift above shoulder height and don't shrug your shoulders up.
Don't lean back or swing to get the weight up.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand, resting in front of your thighs with your palms facing you.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and tighten your stomach.
Raise one arm straight in front of you until it's about level with your shoulder.
Lower it slowly, then repeat with the other arm. You can also raise both together.
watchFor: Don't lean back or swing your body to lift the weight. If you do, it's too heavy.
Stop at shoulder height. Going higher only strains the front of your shoulders.
Use light weights and controlled movements.

steps: Sit at the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand and your feet flat on the floor. Lean forward from your hips until your chest is close to your thighs.
Let the dumbbells hang straight down by your feet with your palms facing each other and a small bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to your sides, leading with your elbows, until they're about level with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a moment.
Lower the dumbbells slowly back down.
watchFor: Use light weights and don't swing your body.
Keep your back flat and your neck in line with your spine.
Don't shrug your shoulders up toward your ears.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, with your palms facing your body.
Keep your arms straight and your chest lifted.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can.
Hold for a moment at the top, then lower them slowly back down.
watchFor: Move only your shoulders. Don't roll them in circles, which can irritate the joint.
Don't bend your elbows to help lift the weight.
Keep your neck long and relaxed and your head still.

steps: Set a cable to the lowest position and attach a single handle. Stand sideways to the machine, holding the handle with the hand farthest from the machine, so the cable crosses in front of you.
Stand up straight with your feet hip-width apart. Keep a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise your arm out to the side until it's about level with your shoulder, leading with your elbow.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly back to the start.
Finish all your reps, then switch sides.
watchFor: Use a light weight. Don't lean or swing to lift it.
Don't raise your arm above shoulder height and don't shrug.
Control the cable on the way down.

steps: Set a cable to about head height and attach a rope handle. Take one end in each hand with your palms facing each other, and step back to lift the weight.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms straight out in front of you.
Pull the rope toward your face, splitting the ends apart as you pull so that your hands end up on either side of your head, level with your ears.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and keep your elbows high.
Slowly straighten your arms again to return to the start.
watchFor: Use a light weight. The goal is a smooth, controlled squeeze, not a heavy pull.
Don't lean back to pull the weight. Keep your body still.
Keep your elbows up at about shoulder level.

steps: Sit at the machine and adjust the seat so the handles are at about shoulder height when you're seated with your back against the pad.
Put your feet flat on the floor and take hold of the handles.
Press the handles upward until your arms are almost straight.
Pause, then lower them slowly back to shoulder height.
watchFor: Keep your back against the pad and don't arch your lower back.
Don't lock your elbows hard at the top.
Don't let the weights slam on the way down.

steps: Sit at the machine and adjust the seat so the pads rest against the outside of your upper arms, just above your elbows.
Sit up straight with your back against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Raise your arms out to your sides by pushing your elbows out and up, until your arms are about level with your shoulders.
Pause, then slowly lower them back down.
watchFor: Don't lean or push with your body. Only your arms should move.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Use a weight you can control on the way down.

steps: Sit facing the machine's pad, with your chest against it, and adjust the seat so the handles are at about shoulder height.
Grab the handles with your arms straight out in front of you and a small bend in your elbows.
Pull the handles back and out to your sides in a wide arc, until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a moment.
Slowly bring the handles back to the start.
watchFor: Keep your chest against the pad and don't shrug your shoulders.
Use a light weight and don't swing.
Don't pull your arms back past your shoulders.

steps: Get on the floor on your hands and feet. Place your hands flat on the floor, a little wider than your shoulders.
Walk your feet toward your hands and lift your hips up high, so your body makes an upside-down V shape, with your legs straight.
Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor in front of your hands, keeping your hips high.
Stop just before your head touches the floor.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight.
watchFor: Don't let your head touch the floor hard. Lower until your head is just above the ground.
Keep your hips high and don't let your body flatten out.
Keep your wrists flat. If your wrists hurt, stop.

steps: Find a clear space near a wall, with no furniture or objects nearby. Put your hands flat on the floor about a hand's length from the wall, a little wider than your shoulders.
Kick your legs up one at a time, with a small hop, until your heels rest lightly against the wall.
Push the floor away with your hands, tighten your stomach and buttocks, and squeeze your legs together so your body is one straight line from your hands to your toes.
Keep your arms locked straight and your head relaxed, looking between your hands.
Hold for the target time, then come down one leg at a time in a controlled way.
watchFor: This is a hard skill. If you've never done it, practice getting up and down a few times before you try holding.
Falling is the main risk, so make sure the area is clear and that you have a plan to come down. If you feel unstable or dizzy, come down right away.
If you have any neck, wrist or shoulder pain, or if you have eye pressure or blood pressure problems, ask a professional first.
